sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 3 / #2 instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice; Internal Quality Checks row 3 - no extra annotation in E:Z; Deterministic Checks C13 says voice is left to the rubric)
evidence: Skill check 2 asks for sentence variety, contractions and occasional terse fragments, and flags uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets or a voice shift between instruction.md and notes. The brief and all three notes keep one consistent first-person firm voice ('we/us/our', with natural slips to 'I' in conversations.md:25,33). It is motivated by situations rather than spec language: instruction.md:1 'our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last', conversations.md:31 'Our internet in court is patchy.', conversations.md:9 'People fix typos and figures', walls-and-retention.md:17 'because a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us', integration.md:5 'we won't run an app that has them'. Contractions are common: doesn't x2 and we'll in instruction.md; can't, mustn't, don't, I've and I'm in conversations.md; isn't, won't, don't and can't in integration.md; aren't and doesn't in walls-and-retention.md. Sentence length varies, from short lines such as 'Everyone signs in with `password123`.' and 'Dev Anand is walled from M-12 today.' up to longer explanatory ones. A grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamline|furthermore|moreover|crucial found nothing, and the brief and notes have 0 bullet or numbered list lines. The only structure is the account table in walls-and-retention.md:5-11, which is reference data, not prose. Residual observation (not a defect): a few passages are dense enumerations, such as the walled-route list at walls-and-retention.md:17, the formatting surfaces at conversations.md:13 and the transcript contents at walls-and-retention.md:35. They are still framed as the firm's own concerns in the same voice and are not marketing or robotic. Counterexample probe: a prompt rewritten as 'The system shall provide a robust, seamless...' with parallel bullets would fail this row, and the current text has none of those markers. Runtime is not relevant to this instruction-only voice row, and no app or Docker run was needed. Pass is the reviewer's judgement on frozen bytes, not a measured portal outcome.
